review_scope: Registered-source content review of On block-wise and reference panel-based estimators for genetic data prediction in high dimensions, by Bingxin Zhao, Shurong Zheng and Hongtu Zhu. The registered 60-page artifact prints arXiv:2203.12003v1 with a 22 March 2022 margin stamp and a 13 June 2025 title-page date. Both dates and the hash remain recorded without resolving the discrepancy by assumption. Main text and references occupy pages 1-27. Only the title heading of the attached Supplementary Material on page 28 was inspected. Fresh text evidence covers all 27 in-scope pages; rendered source and boundary pages were checked against the saved extraction.
inventory: Exactly four main-text Theorems occur: Theorem 1 on pages 8-9, Theorem 2 on pages 9-10, Theorem 3 on page 12 and Theorem 4 on pages 12-13. URWPalladioL-Bold heading enumeration distinguishes these from ordinary-font references on pages 10,12,13. Supplementary results, proofs and differently labelled results are excluded.
original_statements: Theorem 1 preserves Condition 1 and its limiting regime; both zero-limit trace expressions; the quadratic off-block trace with its full factor order; the ordered block-pair sum and o_p(1); the entire Marchenko-Pastur fixed-point equation; and the source names H_l, M_l and m_l. Population Sigma_B_l wording remains literal.

Theorem 2 preserves model (1), Conditions 1-4, the full accuracy ratio including the omega(1-h_beta^2) term, all three R quantities, the unique positive root equation and expectation form, the printed negative-denominator derivative, the maximizing lambda-star assertion and complete optimal accuracy formula (5). The derivative and optimality assertions are transcribed, not repaired or independently proved.

Theorem 3 preserves both trace approximations, their squared factors and denominator corrections, every Sigma versus Sigma-squared factor, and the full K_l definition involving an expected reference trace and companion transform. The printed n^{-1} factors remain unchanged despite the n_w asymptotic regime.

Theorem 4 preserves model (1), Conditions 1,2,3,5, both reference and testing accuracy ratios, all seven Q quantities, the two positive-root equations and the full derivative expression. Q_2 and Q_3 retain the Theorem-3 K_l notation and printed n factors. The second prediction ratio is part of the same theorem, not a separate record.
source_passages: All 23 source entries and eight auxiliary passages were checked. Dataset declarations on pages 4-5 distinguish training/testing responses from the response-free external reference panel. Model (1) retains the shared effect vector and causal coordinates. Random-effect and causal-fraction restrictions remain separate conditions.

Condition 1(a)-(d) preserves standardized innovation designs, finite fourth moments, common positive-definite covariance with dimension-uniform bounds, known aligned blocks, population ESDs and weak limits, and distinct global/block aspect ratios for all three datasets. A detail crop confirms the tilde prefix notation in block indexing. No estimated-block or growing-K theorem is introduced.

Conditions 2 and 3 preserve the causal-fraction interval, p^{-1} effect covariance, independence explicitly stated in the source, and distinct noise variances. The following iid-coordinate interpretation is archived as application context. Genetic heritability remains the realized training signal-energy ratio, not an expected population variance ratio.

The three block covariance constructions and corresponding ridge estimates on page 7 retain their source datasets, aligned columns and sample-size factors. Reference and testing inverses multiply training cross-products, but their printed prefactors are n_w^{-1} and n_z^{-1}. The separate full covariance is the uncentered training Gram matrix. The black-wise typo in the training estimator prose is retained with the display keyword sourced from its heading.

Prediction accuracy on page 8 is the squared uncentered cosine between the testing response and the predicted score. Its instantiations immediately before Theorems 2 and 4 are preserved separately. The definitions do not import centering, intercept fitting or a residual-sum-of-squares metric.

The Stieltjes convention, training sample spectral law and reference-panel companion relation match pages 8 and 12. Population H_l, training M_l/m_l and reference M_w_l/m_w_l/v_w_l remain distinct. The definitions of R/Q, a and K_l are retained in theorem statements or supporting excerpts instead of invented ranked interface names.

Condition 4 contributes both the causal submatrix notation and a separate trace-ratio hypothesis for two listed matrices. Condition 5 reuses that notation with four different matrices. The final matrix in Condition 5 ends in population Sigma; the full testing Gram matrix is defined locally. Neither condition is expanded to all matrices. Discussion-page iid prose and the deferral of alternative effect assumptions to the supplement are preserved without reading the supplement.
dependency_review: All 38 direct uses, 23 reach sets and 53 related connections were checked. Condition 1 and the Stieltjes convention reach all four theorems. The response model, causal fraction, random effects, heritability, accuracy and causal-submatrix notation reach only Theorems 2 and 4. Training block covariance and its sample transform reach Theorems 1 and 2; reference block covariance and companion transform reach Theorems 3 and 4. Testing covariance reaches only Theorem 4. Full training covariance reaches Theorems 1,2,4. Training ridge and Condition 4 reach only Theorem 2; external/testing ridge and Condition 5 reach only Theorem 4. Theorem 4 reuses the K_l definition from Theorem 3 without inheriting its trace conclusions as hypotheses. Trace-only Theorems 1 and 3 acquire no response or ridge-estimation hypotheses.
names_and_highlights: All interfaces use source-derived natural-language keywords and retain their original source headings and kinds. Mathematical symbols are detail selectors, not replacement titles. Population and sample spectral laws, three covariance sources and three ridge constructions remain distinguishable despite shared terminology. Every selector identifies its own source passage/label or an actual related-theorem occurrence, and every related theorem has a source-backed explanation path.
unresolved_scope: There is no required theorem reference whose defining content occurs only in the excluded supplement. Alternative random-effect assumptions mentioned in Section 7 and supplementary proofs remain excluded. The census preserves the source ambiguities in the in-scope statements and does not claim to settle them.
source_limitations: All 28 source notes were reviewed: conflicting source dates; excluded extensions; shared random effects versus cohort independence; array-coupling scope; population standardization versus empirical standardization; known blocks and unspecified block-count growth; empty-prefix indexing; gamma bounds; generic covariance versus iid-coordinate prose; incompletely stated error independence; unequal noise variances versus training heritability; realized heritability and zero-energy cases; squared-cosine interpretation; uncentered covariances; differing ridge normalizations; black-wise spelling; population-block naming; limit-plus-remainder wording; transform domain; derivative sign and variable; asserted optimality; n versus n_w; K_l equality versus deterministic equivalence; listed-matrix homogeneity; the final Condition 5 matrix; test-design reuse; and per-block limit notation. They are recorded separately from the original statements.
changes: No census-content correction was needed. All six saved census JSON artifacts and the historical paper audit remain unchanged. Earlier scripts are archived. The saved paper rebuild resolves the fixed verified PDF, uses saved original transcriptions and regenerates the six artifacts in an empty output directory without old temporary paths or prior output evidence.
validation: Independent inventory and census validators pass, and all six regenerated artifacts match saved bytes. Source hash and both printed dates, complete main-text enumeration and continuation pages, boundary, all direct and local dependency sets, reach sets and paths, selector occurrences and audit artifact hashes supplement the completed manual content review.
